meta.title: noaislop.xyz | your AI slop sucks.
meta.description: A page to send to someone who just published AI slop. This site is not about AI. It’s about effort.
meta.ogDescription: Someone sent you this link. There’s a reason.
meta.ogImageAlt: The word SLOP stamped over a blurred AI answer.

banner: Someone sent you this link. There’s a reason.

definition.text: Low-quality digital content, usually produced in quantity using artificial intelligence.
body: The word got popular in May 2024, thanks to developer Simon Willison. His point was never that AI is bad. Not all AI-generated content is slop. It becomes slop when it’s generated without thinking and pushed onto people who never asked for it.
That’s the whole idea. This site is not about AI. It’s about effort.

cards.prompt: make me a flyer for my event
cards.alt: A chat window. The person asks, in one line, for a flyer for their event. The image that comes back is blurred out and stamped SLOP.

cards.prompt: write me a motivational LinkedIn post about morning coffee
cards.alt: A chat window. The person asks, in one line, for a motivational LinkedIn post about morning coffee. The answer is blurred out and stamped SLOP.
reply: This morning, I poured a cup of coffee. And it taught me everything I need to know about leadership.
Here are the five lessons that changed how I think about building teams, one sip at a time.
What is your morning ritual? Let me know in the comments below.

cards.prompt: make a video of a cat dancing on Survivor
cards.alt: A chat window. The person asks, in one line, for a video of a cat dancing on Survivor. The video that comes back is blurred out and stamped SLOP.

dont.caption: One line in. Zero decisions made. Straight to publish.

cost.lede: You saved four minutes. Everyone else pays for them.

items.title: The feed is finite.
items.text: Every slop post pushes down something someone actually made. People who spent a week on a thing are competing with your four minutes.

items.title: You’re spending our attention, not yours.
items.text: A hundred people read it. That’s hours of collective time, on something nobody thought about for more than a second.

items.title: It’s not free for you either.
items.text: Slop is recognizable. Once people spot it in your work, they start reading everything you publish differently, including the good stuff.

body: AI is a tool. Use it to save time on repetitive, low-value tasks, or to draft something fast and see if the idea holds. That part is fine. But what you publish should always have some of your own brain in it.

blocks.title: Writing
items: The idea is yours. Not “give me 10 post ideas”.
You reread it, and you rewrote it. If the model’s sentence survived untouched, ask yourself why.
Kill the tells. No “it’s not X, it’s Y”. No em dashes everywhere. No “let’s dive in”. No emoji bullet points. No rocket ships.
You can defend every claim in it. Someone replies “where did you get that number?” and you have an answer.

blocks.title: Images
items: You wrote an actual brief, not one line. Composition, framing, colors, what’s in and what’s out.
You gave references. A sketch you made, a mood board, a photo you shot.
You picked a style and named it. If it came out looking like default AI, that’s because you asked for nothing.
You iterated. First output is never the one.

blocks.title: Video
items: AI does a shot you couldn’t get, inside something you actually made.

emphasis: If you don’t put any of yourself into what you post, why should we bother reading it?

test.intro: Before you hit publish, three questions.

items.question: Did you read all of it?
Could you defend it?
items.text: Every claim, every choice. Out loud, to someone who disagrees.

items.question: Would you still publish it if you had to make it by hand?
items.text: If the answer is no, the idea was never worth publishing. The AI didn’t save you time, it just lowered your standards.

test.outro: Three yes. Publish. Otherwise it’s slop.

share.body: Saw an event poster with six fingers on it? A LinkedIn post treating a coffee like a summit push? Drop the link instead of the comment you were about to write.

lines: Spiritual cousin of nohello.net, dontasktoask.com and dontpastetheai.com.
Written by a human, reviewed by a human, defended by a human.
Translations, fixes, PRs welcome on GitHub. Public domain, do what you want with it.
footer.note: If someone sent you this link: they’re not saying you’re a bad creator. They’re saying they’d like to see what you’d have made.
